main_issue: Most evidenced cases are archive-entry Zip Slip/arbitrary-write flows, but the cluster summary also includes infinite-loop/null-or-cycle failures, which are a distinct availability mechanism. The current guideline is additionally broader than the demonstrated archive-extraction evidence by covering arbitrary resource loading, reads, and deletes.
suggested_guideline: For archive extraction, trace attacker-controlled entry names into the resolved extraction target and any subsequent file, directory, symlink, metadata, or output-stream operation. Flag flows where the implementation resolves an entry relative to the extraction root but does not enforce containment of the normalized/canonical target under that root before creating or writing it. Review separator normalization and symlink-aware extraction behavior. A safe fix rejects entries whose resolved destination escapes the intended extraction directory before any filesystem effect.
split_suggestions: Archive extraction path traversal / arbitrary file write through unchecked entry-name containment
Archive-processing denial of service through missing cycle, null, or termination checks
evidence_notes: TestNG evidence directly shows JarEntry names copied to new File(tempDir, jeName) without normalized destination containment validation.
Plexus Archiver evidence directly shows entryName resolved to a target and written, linked, or chmodded without verifying that the target remains under the extraction directory.
DSpace evidence establishes attacker-controlled ZIP input reaching an extraction loop, but the provided excerpt stops before demonstrating the entry-name-to-output-path containment failure.

The one-java-agent, QTIWorks, Goomph, bspkrs, and TJWS examples provide anchors or source-ready provenance but insufficient case-level source behavior to confirm this exact mechanism from the payload alone.

The stated 40-case historical basis and the cluster's infinite-loop variants are not supported by per-case evidence here; they should not remain in the same reusable mechanism group without separate validation.
